title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في تظاهرة حاشدة لجمعية الشبيبة
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at a Packed Event Held by the Youth Association
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ليلة البارحة 8 ديسمبر 2010 محاضرة بعنوان: "الرسالة الدعوية للجمعيات الشبابية "التي نظمتها جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن بساحة فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي بانواكشوط. وكانت التظاهرة حاشدة بجموع غفيرة من جماهير الجمعية وروادها تزاحموا لاستقبال الشيخ والسلام عليه،

وقد ركز فضيلته في المحاضرة على ضرورة سلامة الفكرة وتأسيسها على الأهداف والوسائل الشرعية كبدائل إسلامية في مجال الترفيه، منتقدا من يظنون الترفيه مخالفا للإسلام، حيث قال "إن الجمعيات ينبغي أن تؤسس على أساس راشد لتساهم في خدمة الأوطان الإسلامية... وإن الجهد الجماعي الذي تقدمه الجمعيات والنوادي في البلدان الإسلامية مطلوب شرعا، لأن عمل الكافة لا ينهض إلا بعمل الكافة".

كما ركز الشيخ على أهمية دعوة الشباب الذين قال إنهم عرضة للتشدد والتطرف، كما أنهم عرضة للانحلال والتفريط في الدين.

وقد استعرض الشيخ ذلك من خلال نماذج من حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صحابته؛ حينما بات (ص) ليلة مع صحابته رضوان الله عليهم يستمع للمنشد الذي قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "رفقا بالقوارير"، يقصد قلوب النساء.

وعزز الشيخ الحديث في الموضوع باستشهادات أخرى من حياة الصحابة مع النبي (ص).

كما وجه فضيلته إلى ضرورة جمع جهود هذه الجمعيات الصغيرة في جمعية واحدة كبيرة؛ لتكون أكبر قيمة وأكثر نتاجا.

وتحدث في ذات التظاهرة الشيخ عبد الرحمن ولد فتى الذي أجاد في الحديث عن دور الشباب والأخلاق، والحث على تحمل الأمانة والتحلي بالأخلاق الحميدة.

وكانت الكلمة المؤثرة عند عضو مجلس الشيوخ عمر الفتح؛ الذي دعا الجمعيات الإسلامية إلى الاعتناء بالجماليات في خطابها اتجاه الجماهير، كل حسب ذوقه واهتماماته.
body_en:
Last night, 8 December 2010, his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a lecture entitled "The Mission of Calling to Islam Belonging to Youth Associations", which was organised by the Shabibat Bina' al-Watan Association at the square of the Cultural and Environmental Diversity Space in Nouakchott. The event was packed with great throngs of the association's members and regular attenders, who pressed forward to receive the Sheikh and to greet him.

In the lecture his eminence concentrated on the necessity that the idea be sound and be founded on aims and means that accord with the Sharia, as Islamic alternatives in the field of recreation, criticising those who suppose recreation to be contrary to Islam. He said: "Associations ought to be founded on a rightly guided basis, so that they may contribute to the service of the Muslim homelands… And the collective effort that associations and clubs offer in Muslim countries is called for by the Sharia, because what is the work of all can only be carried through by the work of all."

The Sheikh also concentrated on the importance of calling young people to Islam, of whom he said that they are exposed to harshness and extremism, just as they are exposed to moral dissolution and to falling short in religion.

The Sheikh surveyed this through examples from the life of the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) with his Companions — as when he (peace and blessings be upon him) passed a night with his Companions (may God be pleased with them) listening to the chanter, to whom the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said, "Gently with the glass vessels", meaning the hearts of the women.

The Sheikh strengthened his treatment of the subject with further citations from the life of the Companions with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

His eminence also urged the necessity of gathering the efforts of these small associations into a single large association, so that it may be of greater worth and more productive.

Speaking at the same event was Sheikh Abd al-Rahman Ould Fatta, who spoke ably of the role of young people and of character, and of the call to bear the trust and to adorn oneself with praiseworthy character.

The moving address was that of the senator Umar al-Fath, who called on the Islamic associations to attend to the aesthetic dimension of their discourse towards the public, each according to his own taste and interests.

flags.context: حينما بات (ص) ليلة مع صحابته ... يستمع للمنشد الذي قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم “رفقا بالقوارير”، يقصد قلوب النساء
options: Render the gloss as the source gives it: 'meaning the hearts of the women'
Render as 'meaning the women', the usual understanding
Render the source's gloss and add a note on the usual understanding
flags.note: The gloss 'the hearts of the women' is the site report's, not necessarily the Sheikh's own words. In the standard understanding of this hadith, al-qawārīr — glass vessels — are the women themselves, likened to glass for their delicacy, not their hearts specifically. The source's gloss has been rendered as given rather than corrected, per house rule 11. Note also that the report has the Prophet listening to a chanter through the night, whereas the well-known setting of the hadith is a journey, with Anjashah driving the mounts that carried the women. The report should be checked against the lecture before publication.

flags.context: وإن الجهد الجماعي الذي تقدمه الجمعيات والنوادي في البلدان الإسلامية مطلوب شرعا
options: is called for by the Sharia
flags.note: maṭlūb sharʿan states that the Sharia calls for something without saying at which of the five rulings — obligatory or recommended — it falls. The neutral rendering has been used deliberately so that no ruling is attributed to the Sheikh that he did not give. The following clause about 'the work of all' echoes the language of a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah), but he does not use that term and it has not been supplied.

flags.arabic: جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن / فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي
flags.context: التي نظمتها جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن بساحة فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي بانواكشوط
options: Transliterate the association's name and translate the venue, as done here
Translate both: 'the Youth for Building the Nation Association' at 'the Cultural and Environmental Diversity Space'
flags.note: Both are Mauritanian proper names with no established English form. The association's own English name, if it has one, should be used; the Sheikh's office can confirm.

translator_notes: The CMS does not expose a category or section for this record on the article view, and the 2010 archive is not reachable through the site's section listings. section/category_ar/category_en are therefore left null rather than inferred.

A site news item reporting a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh. The passages in quotation marks are the report's quotation of his words; the rest is the reporter's summary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved — the summarised parts must not be presented as the Sheikh's own wording.
The Sheikh is reported as criticising those who hold recreation to be contrary to Islam. No ruling of his on recreation is stated in this report, and none has been supplied.
The lecture's own title, the Arabic al-risālah al-daʿawiyyah, is rendered 'the mission of calling to Islam' in keeping with the glossary rendering of daʿwah.
